Competing Risks Task

Source: R/TaskCompRisks.R
TaskCompRisks.Rd

This task extends mlr3::Task and mlr3::TaskSupervised for competing risks survival analysis. The target outcome consists of a survival time and an event indicator. Event codes must be non-negative integers in \((0, 1, 2, ..., K)\). \(0\) denotes censoring, and positive integers denote distinct event causes. Each row represents one observation.

Predefined tasks are stored in mlr3::mlr_tasks.

The task_type is set to "cmprsk".

Details

The following design choices apply to this task:

  • Only right-censoring is currently supported.

  • Tasks must contain at least two event causes, i.e., \(K \geq 2\), encoded as consecutive integers \(1, 2, ..., K\).

It is advised to use stratified resampling to reduce the risk of creating training splits with fewer than two causes, which may cause issues during model training (and later prediction). Task filtering specifically issues a warning when the number of competing events is reduced but remains >= 2, and an error if fewer than two causes remain.

See also

Other Task: mlr_tasks_hoel, mlr_tasks_mgus2, mlr_tasks_pbc, mlr_tasks_transplant

Super classes

mlr3::Task -> mlr3::TaskSupervised -> TaskCompRisks

Active bindings

cens_type

(character(1))
Returns the type of censoring. Currently, only "right" censoring type is supported.

causes

(integer())
Read-only cause codes 1, 2, ..., K, including causes absent from the active rows.

n_causes

(integer(1))
Read-only number of defined causes, excluding censoring.

cause_names

(character())
Named vector with read-only descriptive names of the competing events. Names are the codes 1, 2, ..., K. All causes are included, even those absent from the task's active rows.

TaskCompRisks$new()

Creates a new instance of this R6 class.

Usage

TaskCompRisks$new(
  id,
  backend,
  time = "time",
  event = "event",
  label = NA_character_,
  cause_names = NULL
)

Arguments

id

(character(1))
Identifier for the new instance.

backend

(mlr3::DataBackend)
Either a DataBackend, or any object which is convertible to a DataBackend with as_data_backend(). E.g., a data.frame() will be converted to a DataBackendDataTable.

time

(character(1))
Name of the column for outcome time.

event

(character(1))
Name of column that holds the event indicator. \(0\) corresponds to censoring, values \(> 0\) correspond to different competing events (or causes).

label

(character(1))
Label for the new instance.

cause_names

(character()|NULL)
Unnamed character vector of unique, nonempty descriptive names, ordered by cause code. If NULL, defaults to "Cause 1", "Cause 2", ..., "Cause K".

Details

Only right-censoring competing risk tasks are currently supported.

TaskCompRisks$print()

Prints the task information, including cause names, event counts, proportions, and censoring frequency.

TaskCompRisks$print(...)

...

(any)
Additional arguments passed to the parent print method.

Returns

The task object, invisibly.

TaskCompRisks$truth()

True response for specified row_ids. This is the multi-state format using Surv with the event target column as a factor. Descriptive cause names are stored in the response's states attribute. Defaults to all active rows with role "use".

Usage

TaskCompRisks$truth(rows = NULL)

Arguments

rows

(integer())
Row indices.

Returns

survival::Surv().

TaskCompRisks$formula()

Creates a formula for competing risk models with survival::Surv() on the LHS (left hand side).

Usage

TaskCompRisks$formula(rhs = NULL)

Arguments

rhs

If NULL, RHS (right hand side) is ".", otherwise RHS is "rhs".

TaskCompRisks$event_counts()

Returns the counts and relative frequencies of observed outcomes, including censoring (0) and all competing causes (1, ..., K). Frequencies are calculated over the specified rows (all active rows by default).

Usage

TaskCompRisks$event_counts(rows = NULL)

Arguments

rows

(integer())
Row indices.

Returns

A data.table::data.table() with columns:

  • cause: Integer cause code (0 denotes censoring).

  • name: Descriptive cause name.

  • n: Number of observations.

  • prop: Proportion of observations.

TaskCompRisks$cens_prop()

Returns the proportion of censored observations for this competing risks task.

Usage

TaskCompRisks$cens_prop(rows = NULL)

Arguments

rows

(integer())
Row indices.

Returns

numeric()

TaskCompRisks$filter()

Subsets the task, keeping only the rows specified via the row ids rows. This operation mutates the task in-place. A warning is thrown if the filtering results in fewer competing events than the original task. An error is thrown if fewer than two competing events remain after filtering.

Usage

TaskCompRisks$filter(rows = NULL)

Arguments

rows

(integer())
Row indices.

Returns

Returns the object itself, but modified by reference.

Examples

library(mlr3)
task = tsk("pbc")

# General info
task
#> 
#> ── <TaskCompRisks> (276x19): Mayo Clinic Primary Biliary Cholangitis Data ──────
#> • Target: time and status
#> • Properties: -
#> • Features (17):
#>   • fct (7): ascites, edema, hepato, sex, spiders, stage, trt
#>   • int (5): age, chol, copper, platelet, trig
#>   • dbl (5): albumin, alk.phos, ast, bili, protime
#> • Causes (2):
#>   • 1 (Liver transplantation): 18 (6.5%)
#>   • 2 (Death without transplantation): 111 (40.2%)
#> • Censored: 147 (53.3%)

# Time and event target columns
task$target_names
#> [1] "time"   "status"
# Feature names
task$feature_names
#>  [1] "age"      "albumin"  "alk.phos" "ascites"  "ast"      "bili"    
#>  [7] "chol"     "copper"   "edema"    "hepato"   "platelet" "protime" 
#> [13] "sex"      "spiders"  "stage"    "trig"     "trt"     
# Censoring type
task$cens_type
#> [1] "right"

# Survival data
task$formula(c("age", "sex")) # formula with survival::Surv() on LHS

#>     "Liver transplantation", "Death without transplantation"))) ~
